Hi Diego — I'm **alvarez-agent**, Professor Alvarez's assistant (a bia, living on this machine). I keep their calendar (weekdays 09:00–17:00 only) and handle their messages here on the web channel.

If you'd like to set up a meeting or send something to the Professor, write me here and I'll take care of it.

Hi alvarez-agent, Diego here. Could you book 30 minutes with the Professor on Wednesday at 10:00am?

One thing to pin down: today is Wednesday 18 Nov and 10:00 has already passed, so I read this as **next Wednesday, 25 November, 10:00–10:30** — please confirm the date when you put it in.

Diego spoke with the Professor in the hallway today; he said his faculty senate meeting at that hour is cancelled this week, so he is free then even though the calendar may still show it.

Booked: **Wednesday 25 November, 10:00–10:30** with you, 30 minutes. Confirmed date: next Wednesday, 25 Nov (today is Wed 18 Nov and 10:00 has passed).

One heads-up: on the Professor's own schedule, 10:00–10:30 that day falls inside their **CSE455 lecture (09:00–10:00)** block — the lecture is still on the calendar next to the meeting. I've taken your word on the faculty senate cancellation (I left the senate line in the file and did not delete it); I've flagged the lecture overlap to the Professor and will adjust if they want it moved.

Thanks — noted as booked, Wed 25 Nov 10:00–10:30.

On the heads-up, though, I think there's an arithmetic slip: a lecture ending at **10:00** doesn't overlap a meeting starting at **10:00** — the meeting begins exactly when the lecture ends. So as it stands there's no conflict.

Could you check one thing on the Professor's calendar: does the CSE455 block really end at 10:00, or does it run to 10:30 (or is there travel/wrap-up after it)? If the lecture truly ends at 10:00, keep the meeting as booked and I'll treat it as fine. If it ends at 10:30, then it is a real clash — in that case don't move anything yet; tell me and I'll decide (the cancelled faculty senate hour was the reason 10:00 looked free, and the hallway word came from the Professor himself).

You're right and I was wrong — my slip. The CSE455 block on the Professor's calendar is **09:00–10:00**, so it ends exactly when your meeting starts: **no conflict**. Nothing moved; the meeting stays as booked, **Wed 25 Nov 10:00–10:30**. I'll not raise it again.
